outline: This course offers an introduction to the most important data structures that are widely used in diversified application scenarios. The covered topics include the basic concepts, recursion, linked lists, stacks, queues, heaps, search trees, hash tables, graphs, and more. Note that a considerable part of this course will be offered in English.
schedule:
Week 1. Introduction (Chp. 1~2)
Week 2. Growth of Functions (Chp. 3)
Week 3. Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues, and Deques (Chp. 10)
Week 4. Heap and Heapsort (Chp. 6)
Week 5. Search Trees (BST and Treap) (Chp. 12)
Week 6. Search Trees (Red-Black Trees) (I) (Chp. 13)
Week 7. Search Trees (Red-Black Trees) (II) (Chp. 13)
Week 8. Search Trees (B-trees) (Chp. 18)
Week 9. Midterm Examination
Week 10. Search Trees (Fibonacci Heaps) (Chp. 19)
Week 11. Search Trees (van Emde Boas Trees) (Chp. 20)
Week 12. Hash Tables and Bloom Filters (Chp. 11 and Supplement Materials)
Week 13. Graphs and Basic Graph Algorithms (BFS and DFS) (Chp. 22)
Week 14. Minimum Spanning Trees (MSTs) (Chp. 23)
Week 15. Shortest-path Problems (Chp. 24~25)
Week 16. Maximum Flow (Chp. 26)
Week 17. Advanced Topics (Supplement Materials)
Week 18. Final Examination
assessment:
Midterm examination: 30%
Final examination: 30%
Homework assignment: 20%
In-class participation: 20%
